To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ethical and social aspects of virtual knowledge should be considered in the context of online communities and their norms, values, and practices, as these are the main sources for the justification and the production of online knowledge.

the online communities are a new type of social group, which is characterized by the absence of a face-to-face communication, the existence of a shared goal, the use of the Internet and the presence of the community members on a regular basis.

the online communities are a new form of knowledge production and that their knowledge is not only virtual but also real, and that they are a new form that is not only a new form of communication and interaction, but also a new form of social organization.
In summary, our research is concerned with

how online communities can be understood as a new form of social knowledge, which is not only a new way of sharing and producing knowledge, but also a new way of justifying knowledge claims, and, in particular, how this new form of knowledge and justification is related to the moral and ethical responsibility of its participants and the community itself.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
online technologies have a strong ethical and moral impact on our lives.

the online community is not a mere aggregation of individuals but a new kind of social reality, which is not a mere extension of the real world, but rather a new kind of reality, with a new kind of knowledge, and a new kind of responsibility.

online knowledge is genuine knowledge if it is the outcome of a community that is committed to the same epistemic norms and values as the ones that are accepted in the traditional epistemic communities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the online communities have a special status in the sense of the social and cultural context in which they emerge, as well as in the sense of a special type of community.

we have been able to identify the main problems that arise when we deal with the online knowledge, and we have proposed a new way to understand the notion of online community and its ethical and normative implications.

we have tried to show how the online world can be a source of new knowledge, which has a different structure from the one we are familiar with in the real world, and that it is possible to develop a normative code for the online community.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to develop new forms of justification for online knowledge, which can be seen as a form of knowledge that can be justified by the community of practice, and not by the individual.
the online communities, as well as the technologies, are not value-neutral, but they can be used for good or for evil.
online technologies have a strong influence over the way we perceive the world, and the way we act in it.
